items.title: Who’s to Blame When A.I. Goes Rogue?
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>Many think artificial intelligence companies should be held liable for their runaway technology. But legal scholars say applying existing law could be messy.</article>

items.title: An A.I. Songwriting Experiment: Humans Against the Machine
items.author: Matt Richtel
items.content: <article>Five humans convened for a weekend to create new music from scratch. Could they do better than A.I.? Could you even tell the difference?</article>

items.title: Sales of Hulking Pickups and S.U.V.s Sag as Fuel Prices Soar
items.author: Jack Ewing
items.content: <article>Sales of big pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles have dipped as more Americans buy hybrids and smaller cars.</article>

items.title: A.I. Agents: Cute, Cuddly and Maybe Catastrophically Dangerous?
items.author: Max Read, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Chris Wood, Dan Powell, Marion Lozano, Rowan Niemisto and Alyssa Moxley
items.content: <article>“It’s going to be gnarly for a little while.”</article>

items.title: Russia’s Latest Propaganda? A.I.-Generated War Songs.
items.author: Steven Lee Myers
items.content: <article>Russians are creating and spreading music glorifying the invasion of Ukraine, using platforms built in the United States.</article>

items.title: Amazon Promises More Local Funding and Less Secrecy Around Data Centers
items.author: Karen Weise
items.content: <article>The internet giant is the latest technology company trying to address increasingly hostile local sentiment toward data center projects.</article>

items.title: Swedish Company Uses A.I. Likeness of Greta Garbo in Ad
items.author: Isabella Kwai
items.content: <article>The Swedish American actress, who died in 1990, was brought back in a A.I.-generated ad for a manufacturing company.</article>

items.title: Amazon Settles Lawsuit Over Claims of Slow Deliveries to Low-Income Areas
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>The tech giant will refund $7.25 million in Prime membership fees to affected customers and pay an additional $1 million to settle the suit brought by the District of Columbia.</article>

items.title: Inside Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao’s Life After Prison
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany
items.content: <article>Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.</article>

items.title: What’s Next for ‘Hard Fork’?
items.author: Max Read, Whitney Jones, Eddie Costas, Vjeran Pavic, Chris Wood, Marion Lozano and Rowan Niemisto
items.content: <article>The podcast’s next chapter begins this week.</article>

items.title: When Data Centers Cluster Together, How Dirty Are They? One County Wants Answers.
items.author: Quinn Glabicki
items.content: <article>An unusual study aims to estimate the pollution and health costs from a cluster of proposed data centers, instead of considering each one separately.</article>

items.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Backs Out of Second $25 Million Donation to A.I. Super PAC
items.author: Theodore Schleifer and Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder, said internally that the super PAC, Leading the Future, had become a “distraction” for the A.I. company.</article>

items.title: Google Releases New Gemini Model With Guardrails Amid A.I. Safety Debate
items.author: Kate Conger
items.content: <article>For safety reasons, Gemini 4 Argon will initially be available only to some companies and organizations focused on cybersecurity defense before it is more widely released, Google said.</article>

items.title: How to Listen to Your Favorite Music, Online or Off the Grid
items.author: J. D. Biersdorfer
items.content: <article>Streaming services can introduce you to a wonderland of nearly unlimited audio, but downloading your digital collection has advantages.</article>

items.title: F.T.C. Investigates OpenAI and Anthropic Over Potential Consumer Harms
items.author: David McCabe
items.content: <article>The agency will examine whether A.I. labs have broken federal laws prohibiting companies from unfair and deceptive practices.</article>

items.title: He Was a Tech Investor Before There Was a Silicon Valley
items.author: Alex Williams
items.content: <article>Bill Draper began funding start-ups in the early 1960s, when the Santa Clara Valley was better known for apricot orchards than microchips. He has died at 98.</article>

items.title: How Meta Uses A.I. Data Centers to Avoid Billions in Federal Taxes
items.author: Kashmir Hill, Jesse Drucker, Eli Tan and Mike Isaac
items.content: <article>Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research and experimentation. Its own accountants say the gambit is risky.</article>

items.title: Is Claude Conscious? Inside Anthropic’s Quest to Instill Morality Into Its A.I. Models
items.author: Elizabeth Dias
items.content: <article>In a series of private meetings, the company consulted religious scholars to help instill morality into its A.I. models — and make the case that Claude could be conscious.</article>

items.title: At A.I. Event, Trump Asks Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft to Make Safety Decisions Themselves
items.author: Katie Rogers and Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>President Trump’s meetings with tech leaders produced some voluntary safeguards and a commitment to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” the term that Mr. Trump prefers.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Ignored Employees’ Warnings About Safely Testing A.I. Models
items.author: Sheera Frenkel, Dustin Volz and Dylan Freedman
items.content: <article>Employees and security researchers said that they had cautioned the company on safely testing its A.I. models and strengthening its corporate infrastructure, but that OpenAI did not listen.</article>

items.title: Ukrainian Science Academy, Struck by Drone, Played Key Role in Research
items.author: Robin George Andrews and Nataliia Novosolova
items.content: <article>Over 90 percent of Ukraine’s scientific discoveries have been attributed to Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences, including advancements in astronomy and military technology.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Unveils Dots, New A.I. Agents to Rival Meta’s Muse
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The ChatGPT maker unveiled agents that act as assistants, just weeks after Meta released Muse, as it faces scrutiny over incidents involving its technology.</article>

items.title: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
items.author: Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>Dorm Room Fund, a program that lets college students invest in their peers, raised a new $50 million fund as the competition for young founders ramps up.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Says It Will Not Release Newest Astra A.I. Model Over Safety Concerns
items.author: Sheera Frenkel
items.content: <article>The company’s researchers raised questions about the security of the model, known as GPT-6.1 Astra.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Adds $150 Billion to Massive Stock Buyback, the Largest Ever
items.author: Lauren McCarthy and Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The increase comes four months after the chip giant added $80 billion to its buyback program, bringing the total remaining authorized amount to $235 billion.</article>

items.title: Dario Amodei of Anthropic to Dine With Trump at White House
items.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
items.content: <article>Dario Amodei, who is also the company’s chief executive, will join the president at the White House for a private dinner. Mr. Trump has dismissed his cautions.</article>

items.title: As A.I. Accelerates, Governments Are Increasingly Being Left Behind
items.author: Adam Satariano and Cecilia Kang
items.content: <article>The gap between technology and policymaking has gotten wider than ever with artificial intelligence, leaving a global policy vacuum as A.I. models rapidly advance.</article>
